975: Storage period altered ash to a highly significant degree. In order of sampling, the values were 0.800% in fresh paddy, 0.780% at 4 months, 0.772% at 8 months and 0.779% at 12 months, fresh paddy returning the highest value and 8 months the lowest. By the close of the year the value had declined by 2.7%.
977: The location × variety interaction was significant at the 1% level. Radhunipagal at Nadia constituted the superior combination with 1.161%, and Gobindabhog at Nadia the inferior one with 0.368%. Rank order varied with location: at Nadia the ranking ran Radhunipagal, Kalojira, Gobindabhog; at Purba Bardhaman, Kalojira, Gobindabhog, Radhunipagal; and at Birbhum/Howrah, Kalojira, Radhunipagal, Gobindabhog. Such reordering establishes that the landraces responded to their environments to differing degrees.
978: The location × storage interaction was significant at the 1% level. The highest mean, 0.866%, was recorded for Nadia in fresh paddy and the lowest, 0.672%, for Purba Bardhaman at 8 months. Between fresh paddy and 12 months of storage the change amounted to -7.0% at Nadia, -1.6% at Purba Bardhaman and +0.8% at Birbhum/Howrah, a spread of 7.8 percentage points, with grain from Nadia changing most and that from Birbhum/Howrah least. The rate of change during storage was therefore not uniform across grain of the three provenances.
979: The variety × storage interaction was highly significant. The highest mean, 0.991%, was recorded for Kalojira in fresh paddy and the lowest, 0.581%, for Gobindabhog at 8 months. Over the year Gobindabhog changed by -4.4%, Radhunipagal by -3.8% and Kalojira by -0.8%, Gobindabhog shifting furthest and Kalojira least. The three landraces consequently did not gain or lose at equivalent rates during storage.
980: The three factors interacted significantly. Among the thirty six treatment combinations, the maximum value of 1.249% was recorded by Radhunipagal grown at Nadia and sampled as fresh paddy, and the minimum of 0.350% by Gobindabhog grown at Nadia and likewise sampled as fresh paddy, a spread of 0.899 percentage points. This range far exceeded that generated by any single factor in isolation; the effect proceeded from the three factors in conjunction, and all three required appropriate specification to secure the optimum outcome.
989: Ash denotes the residue remaining after combustion of the grain and represents its total mineral content. Verma and Srivastav (2017) likewise recorded substantial differences in ash among Indian aromatic rices and reported aromatic types to be superior to non-aromatic ones on this count. Patra et al. (2024) similarly obtained higher ash in Tulaipanji grain from West Bengal where the crop was raised on organic nutrient sources, which indicates that ash responds to soil supply as well as to landrace. Ash would not be expected to alter appreciably during storage, since minerals are neither generated nor lost from grain held in store; the effect registers as significant here only because the coefficient of variation for this trait, at 0.23%, was unusually low. The most plausible explanation is that ash was computed on a fresh weight basis and therefore shifts marginally as grain moisture fluctuates.
993: Location exerted a highly significant effect on total phenol. The highest value, 0.8232 mg GAE/g, was recorded at Birbhum/Howrah, followed by Nadia with 0.7145 mg GAE/g and Purba Bardhaman with 0.4614 mg GAE/g. All three locations were statistically discrete, differing significantly among themselves, and the gap between the superior and inferior sites amounted to 0.3617 mg GAE/g.
995: The three landraces likewise differed, the varietal effect being highly significant. Kalojira recorded the highest value, 0.7812 mg GAE/g, followed by Radhunipagal with 0.6459 mg GAE/g and Gobindabhog with 0.5719 mg GAE/g. The three landraces resolved into discrete groups, Kalojira exceeding Gobindabhog by 0.2093 mg GAE/g.
997: Storage period altered total phenol significantly at the 1% level. In order of sampling, the values were 0.8868 mg GAE/g in fresh paddy, 0.7590 mg GAE/g at 4 months, 0.5976 mg GAE/g at 8 months and 0.4220 mg GAE/g at 12 months, the peak occurring in fresh paddy and the trough at 12 months. Across the twelve months the value declined by 52.4%.
999: The location × variety interaction was highly significant. Kalojira at Birbhum/Howrah constituted the superior combination with 0.9337 mg GAE/g, and Gobindabhog at Purba Bardhaman the inferior one with 0.3891 mg GAE/g. The varietal rank order — Kalojira first, Radhunipagal second, Gobindabhog third — held at every location; only the width of the varietal difference shifted, its direction remaining unaffected.
1000: The location × storage interaction was highly significant. The highest mean, 1.0966 mg GAE/g, was recorded for Birbhum/Howrah in fresh paddy and the lowest, 0.3237 mg GAE/g, for Purba Bardhaman at 12 months. Between harvest and 12 months the change amounted to -54.9% at Nadia, -46.4% at Purba Bardhaman and -53.6% at Birbhum/Howrah, a spread of 8.5 percentage points, with grain from Nadia changing most and that from Purba Bardhaman least. The rate of change during storage was therefore not uniform across grain of the three provenances.
1001: The variety × storage interaction attained the 1% level. The highest mean, 1.0325 mg GAE/g, was recorded for Kalojira in fresh paddy and the lowest, 0.3620 mg GAE/g, for Gobindabhog at 12 months. Twelve months of storage yielded changes of -53.0% in Gobindabhog, -53.1% in Radhunipagal and -51.4% in Kalojira. The three landraces shifted by nearly equivalent margins, storage having affected them comparably.
1002: The L × V × S interaction was highly significant. Among the thirty six treatment combinations, the maximum value of 1.2632 mg GAE/g was recorded by Kalojira grown at Birbhum/Howrah and sampled as fresh paddy, and the minimum of 0.2734 mg GAE/g by Gobindabhog grown at Purba Bardhaman and sampled at 12 months, a spread of 0.9898 mg GAE/g. This range substantially exceeded that attributable to any individual factor; all three factors operated jointly, and the optimum outcome was contingent upon the correct specification of each.
1011: Phenolic compounds constitute the principal health-promoting substances in rice. They scavenge free radicals in vivo and account in large measure for the value attributed to pigmented rices. The differentiation between locations was unusually pronounced, Birbhum and Howrah returning nearly twice the phenol content of Purba Bardhaman. A margin of this magnitude indicates that growing conditions exert a powerful influence on the accumulation of phenolic material in the grain. Zhang et al. (2010) demonstrated that black rice bran carries far greater phenolic content than unpigmented rice, and Shao et al. (2014) quantified the distribution of these compounds between the bran, embryo and endosperm of white, red and black rice. Conventional storage in West Bengal approximates the warmer of those two regimes, which may partly explain the severity of the loss recorded here.
1015: Location exerted a highly significant effect on total flavonoid. The highest value, 19.09 mg QE/100 g, was recorded at Birbhum/Howrah, followed by Nadia with 16.74 mg QE/100 g and Purba Bardhaman with 12.07 mg QE/100 g. No two locations shared a letter group, each therefore standing apart from the remaining two, and the gap between the superior and inferior sites amounted to 7.02 mg QE/100 g.
1017: Varietal differences were equally distinct, attaining significance at the 1% level. Kalojira recorded the highest value, 18.06 mg QE/100 g, followed by Radhunipagal with 15.86 mg QE/100 g and Gobindabhog with 13.98 mg QE/100 g. All three landraces were statistically discrete, Kalojira exceeding Gobindabhog by 4.08 mg QE/100 g.
1019: Storage period altered total flavonoid significantly at the 1% level. In order of sampling, the values were 19.57 mg QE/100 g in fresh paddy, 17.14 mg QE/100 g at 4 months, 14.87 mg QE/100 g at 8 months and 12.28 mg QE/100 g at 12 months, fresh paddy standing highest and the 12-month sample lowest. The value declined by 37.3% over the year.
1021: The location × variety interaction was non-significant. Kalojira at Birbhum/Howrah constituted the superior combination with 21.19 mg QE/100 g, and Gobindabhog at Purba Bardhaman the inferior one with 10.32 mg QE/100 g. The three landraces retained an identical order — Kalojira, Radhunipagal, Gobindabhog — at each location; the interaction therefore modified the magnitude of the varietal differences rather than their direction.
1022: The location × storage term fell short of significance. The highest mean, 22.87 mg QE/100 g, was recorded for Birbhum/Howrah in fresh paddy and the lowest, 8.41 mg QE/100 g, for Purba Bardhaman at 12 months. By 12 months the three districts had changed by -35.1%, -46.2% and -33.1% respectively. All three locations shifted by closely comparable margins, the effect of storage proving independent of the district of origin.
1023: The variety × storage term likewise fell short of significance. The highest mean, 21.80 mg QE/100 g, was recorded for Kalojira in fresh paddy and the lowest, 10.38 mg QE/100 g, for Gobindabhog at 12 months. Across twelve months Gobindabhog changed by -40.6%, Radhunipagal by -36.2% and Kalojira by -35.5%. All three changed by comparable margins and thus responded to storage in a uniform manner.
1024: The three-factor interaction was non-significant. Among the thirty six treatment combinations, the maximum value of 25.16 mg QE/100 g was recorded by Kalojira grown at Birbhum/Howrah and sampled as fresh paddy, and the minimum of 6.52 mg QE/100 g by Gobindabhog grown at Purba Bardhaman and sampled at 12 months. Given the non-significance of this term, these extreme cells cannot be interpreted as genuine differences in isolation, and the main effects afford the more reliable inference.
1033: Flavonoids constitute one family within the broader group of phenolic compounds and account for much of the antioxidant activity of pigmented grain. Plants accumulate flavonoids partly in response to stress imposed by intense insolation, drought or impoverished soil, so a harsher growing environment frequently yields grain richer in these compounds even where it yields less grain overall. The probable explanation is that many grain flavonoids carry attached sugar moieties, which renders them more stable against oxidation than simple phenolic acids. Kunnam et al. (2023) identified environment as the principal source of variation in the phenolic fraction of rice across locations, and Naveed et al. (2023) recorded losses of antioxidant constituents of up to 50% over six months of storage; the flavonoid data obtained here conform to both patterns.
1037: Location exerted a highly significant effect on antioxidant capacity. The highest value, 41.35 mg TE/100 g, was recorded at Birbhum/Howrah, followed by Nadia with 34.83 mg TE/100 g and Purba Bardhaman with 28.73 mg TE/100 g. The three locations resolved into discrete groups, each differing significantly from the others, and the gap between the superior and inferior sites amounted to 12.62 mg TE/100 g.
1039: Varietal differences were equally distinct, attaining significance at the 1% level. Kalojira recorded the highest value, 40.26 mg TE/100 g, followed by Radhunipagal with 34.74 mg TE/100 g and Gobindabhog with 29.91 mg TE/100 g. All three landraces were statistically discrete, Kalojira exceeding Gobindabhog by 10.34 mg TE/100 g.
1041: Storage period altered antioxidant capacity to a highly significant degree. In order of sampling, the values were 53.44 mg TE/100 g in fresh paddy, 38.95 mg TE/100 g at 4 months, 27.57 mg TE/100 g at 8 months and 19.92 mg TE/100 g at 12 months, the maximum falling on fresh paddy and the minimum on 12 months. A decline of 62.7% was registered over the full year.
1043: Location and variety did not operate independently, their interaction being highly significant. Kalojira at Birbhum/Howrah constituted the superior combination with 45.63 mg TE/100 g, and Gobindabhog at Purba Bardhaman the inferior one with 24.69 mg TE/100 g. The varietal order Kalojira, Radhunipagal, Gobindabhog remained invariant across locations; the interaction therefore altered the magnitude of the varietal margin but not its sign.
1044: The location × storage interaction attained the 1% level. The highest mean, 62.11 mg TE/100 g, was recorded for Birbhum/Howrah in fresh paddy and the lowest, 13.57 mg TE/100 g, for Purba Bardhaman at 12 months. From fresh paddy to 12 months the value shifted by -61.2% at Nadia, -70.4% at Purba Bardhaman and -58.3% at Birbhum/Howrah, a spread of 12.1 percentage points, with grain from Purba Bardhaman changing most and that from Birbhum/Howrah least. The rate of change during storage was therefore not uniform across grain of the three provenances.
1045: Variety and storage period did not act independently. The highest mean, 61.13 mg TE/100 g, was recorded for Kalojira in fresh paddy and the lowest, 16.26 mg TE/100 g, for Gobindabhog at 12 months. The twelve-month change amounted to -63.8% in Gobindabhog, -64.6% in Radhunipagal and -60.2% in Kalojira, Radhunipagal shifting furthest and Kalojira least. The three landraces therefore did not gain or lose at equivalent rates during storage.
